summary: Greg Bailey is an Indology scholar who earned his PhD in Indian Studies at the University of Melbourne in 1980 under J. Durham and Madeleine Biardeau. He was a visiting research fellow at the University of Tübingen (1998) and a professor at La Trobe University.

Gregor Ahn is a scholar of religious studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Copenhagen and Bonn (Magister 1986, PhD 1991 under Hans-Joachim Klimkeit, Habilitation 1995). He held posts at Münster (1992–1994) and served as Professor at Heidelberg University (1996–2025).

Gregorio Franzò was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Pisa and Scuola Normale Superiore from 1901 to 1904, and later taught "materie letterarie" as a professor at Liceo Classico Carducci Ricasoli.

Gregory Adam Scott works in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Columbia University and holds posts as Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester and at the University of Edinburgh (both attested 2026).

Gregory Forgues is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher (attested 2011) and later studied under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, serving as a researcher and translator at Dharmamitra (attested 2026).

Gregory Hillis is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He completed an MA at the University of Virginia in 1993, later held a post there (attested 2002), and is a Continuing Lecturer at UC Santa Barbara (attested 2026).

Gregory L. Possehl was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago and studied under Walter A. Fairservis, Jr., later serving as Professor at the University of Pennsylvania and Curator at its Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology.

Gregory Max Seton specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Naropa University, UC Santa Barbara (MA 2008), and Oxford (Wolfson College, D.Phil 2015), supervised by Vesna Wallace and Alexis Sanderson.
Gregory Nagy is a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington (~1958–1962) and Harvard University (~1962–1966), where he held a post in 2025.

Gregory P. A. Levine works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Oberlin College (1985) and Princeton University (1990, 1997), and became an Associate Professor of Art and Architecture of Japan at UC Berkeley (~2003).

Gregory Price Grieve works in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from San Francisco State and the University of Chicago (PhD ~2002), later lecturing at Chicago (1998) and DePaul (2001) before becoming Professor and Department Head at UNC Greensboro (2002).

Gregory Schopen specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the Australian National University (~1975–1978) under Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana, later holding professorships at the University of Texas at Austin (~1989–1999) and UCLA (~1999–2019).

Grigorij Fedorovich Ilyin was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Moscow State University under Igor Mikhailovich Reisner, later working at the Diplomatic Academy (1947–1953), the Institute of History of the Academy of Sciences (1952), and the University of Chicago (1953).

Grigorij Lukich Nakhutsrishvili was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Tbilisi State University (~1944–1949), where he later taught from 1952 and became chair in 1976.

Grigory Maksimovich Bongard-Levin was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the MSU Institute of Asian and African Studies under George de Roerich, and held posts at Moscow State University (~1962–2008) and the Russian Academy of Sciences.

Gritli von Mitterwallner was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her Dr. phil. (1964) and Habilitation (~1964–1971) at the University of Munich, where she later served as Professor from 1978 to 1991.
Gu Rong Gyalsé Chökyi Lodrö studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Gualtherus Hendrik Mees was a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Cambridge (~1924–1928), under Jean Philippe Vogel, and completed an LL.D. at Leiden University (~1929–1935).

Guang Xing is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at SOAS University of London (~1999–2003) under Tadeusz Skorupski and Timothy Hugh Barrett. He held posts at the University of Hong Kong (~2003) and the University of British Columbia (2007).

Guangchang Fang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He held a research post at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1986–2000) and later served as a professor at Shanghai Normal University (~2006).
